findings.title: Date override day short-circuits the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot falls inside the override window, the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `undefined` for that override, so the outer `if` is false and execution reaches `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` (line 133-135). This returns early and completely skips the `busy.every(...)` loop below, meaning existing bookings, calendar busy times and buffers are ignored for any day that has a date override. Users can therefore be double-booked on date-override days. The override check should only decide whether the slot is inside the override window; the busy check must still run afterwards.

findings.title: Working-hours check computes `end` from the slot start instead of the slot end
findings.body: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` computation on the previous line; `slotEndTime` is never used. As a result the check `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them, so slots that overrun the end of the organizer's availability (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 15 minutes before the schedule ends) are still reported as available.

findings.title: Working-hours predicate marks a slot unavailable if ANY working-hour range does not contain it
findings.body: The new check uses `workingHours.find(workingHour => ... if (start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime) return true)` and then treats a match as "slot is outside of working hours" -> unavailable. Because `find` succeeds as soon as one range does not contain the slot, any schedule with more than one availability range applicable to the same weekday (split days such as 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00, or ranges split across UTC midnight by `getWorkingHours`) will cause every slot to be rejected, producing an empty schedule. The predicate must instead require that *no* range contains the slot (e.g. `!workingHours.some(wh => wh.days.includes(day) && start >= wh.startTime && end <= wh.endTime)`).

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with `===`, condition is always false
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two freshly constructed Dayjs objects by reference, which is never true. The intended check (a zero-length override, i.e. a day marked unavailable) is therefore dead code; such overrides are only handled accidentally by the later `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)` branch, and a slot exactly at the override instant would be treated as available. Use `.isSame()` on the two values.

findings.title: Timezone-shifted date override wraps around midnight and silently loses availability
findings.body: The override start/end are converted to minutes-of-day with `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`. When the invitee/organizer offset difference pushes the override across a day boundary (e.g. organizer 22:00-23:00 with a +8h invitee, or 02:00 with a -5h invitee), `hour()` wraps to the other day, so `startTime` can become greater than `endTime`. `buildSlots` then drops such a range via its `if (start >= end) continue` guard (or produces slots at completely wrong times), so the override silently yields no availability for invitees in far-away timezones.

findings.title: Override offset depends on an optional `timeZone` that falls back to the server timezone
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` is used to compute the organizer offset, but `TimeRange.timeZone` is declared optional in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`. If any caller of `getSlots` passes date overrides without `timeZone` (only the slots router was updated to attach it), `dayjs.tz(undefined)` resolves to the dayjs default/system timezone, producing a wrong organizer offset and silently shifted override slots instead of an error. Either make `timeZone` required for the overrides consumed here or explicitly fall back to the organizer timezone already passed into `getSlots`.

findings.title: No test covers the main fix (date overrides of fixed hosts in round-robin) and the new timezone test is not sensitive to the organizer timezone
findings.body: The PR's primary change is that fixed-host date overrides are honoured for ROUND_ROBIN events (via the new `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` arguments to `checkIfIsAvailable`), but no test creates a round-robin event with a fixed host that has a date override, so that code path is unverified. The added test only re-requests the same personal event with a different invitee timezone and asserts identical UTC slots; it does not exercise an organizer whose schedule timezone differs from the invitee's, and it does not cover a day that has both a date override and an existing booking (where the current implementation returns the slot as available).
